incident-bot: URGENT: Elevated 5xx rate observed for private-inference-gateway-prod (route: private/v1/generate). Current 5m error rate 18%. Paging on-call: @Nina :rotating_light:

Nina (oncall): ACKing. I'm on it. First check: are health checks failing on the gateway ALB or backend pool?

Ashley (eng): ALB target health looks mostly healthy but we're seeing a spike in 502/504 from the gateway itself. Logs show upstream connection resets. sample log: `502 GET /private/v1/generate - upstream read error: read timeout`

Nina (oncall): I ran a quick curl from a debug pod in the same VPC:
```
curl -v https://private-gateway.prod.redwood.internal/private/v1/health
* Connected to private-gateway.prod.redwood.internal (10.12.5.8) port 443 (#0)
> GET /private/v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: private-gateway.prod.redwood.internal

< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json

{"error":"upstream read timeout"}
```

Nina (oncall): I also checked NAT gateway metrics in CloudWatch — SNAT port utilization is spiking in us-west-2b. NATGatewayId: nat-0a1b2c3d. TODO: confirm ephemeral port exhaustion or conntrack limits.

Mike (netops): Seeing unusual peering flaps for the VPC peering connection pcx-0f9e8d7c between vpc-frontend-prod and vpc-inference-prod. AWS console shows status "available" but CloudWatch PeerStatusChange logs show transitions: AVAILABLE -> DELETING -> AVAILABLE in short window. Possible control-plane retries.

Leila (sre): Can you run conntrack and nat port checks on the gateway nodes (if using NAT instances) or check NAT gateway metric `ActiveConnections`? Commands if nat instance:
```
sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
ss -s | grep -i established
```
If NAT gateway service, check CloudWatch metric `ActiveFlowCount` and `BytesOut`.

Mike (netops): Confirmed: ActiveFlowCount for nat-0a1b2c3d in us-west-2b at 98% of baseline and ephemeral port utilization at 65k/65535 in Console. That smells like port depletion.

Grace (support): Impact note: Support ticket bucket shows ~120 customers experiencing 502s starting ~1918765400. Customer-facing impact: inference requests failing intermittently (timeouts/5xx). We should prepare a short status update for customers.

Nina (oncall): Quick mitigations I'm testing now:
- Spin up a new NAT gateway in us-west-2a and update route table for subnet private-inference-subnet-a to point to new NAT (fast failover)
- Restart a subset of gateway workers to re-establish connections (canary 2 nodes)
- Enable short-term retries on the edge LB (5xx backoff)

netops-bot: Action issued: create-nat(nat-1) in us-west-2a [IN PROGRESS]

Ashley (eng): For immediate relief, we can also switch a portion of traffic to hosted inference fallback for affected customers (route policy: if private gateway 5xx > 5% then route to hosted). Want to avoid if possible but it's available.

Mike (netops): There's another signal: VPC peering connection logs show increased "PacketReject" entries correlated with SG egress policy change that was rolled out at 1918765200. Was anyone changing SGs?

Leila (sre): @Ashley did your team modify any outbound rules recently? Even a narrow egress change could cause intermittent resets if NAT/prefixing changed.

Ashley (eng): We rolled a tighter egress rule to lock down external telemetry at 1918765150 but it targeted a different security group. I'll double-check dependencies.

Nina (oncall): Running tcpdump on gateway ENI to see RSTs and retransmits. Snippet:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.9.2.14 and port 443 -w /tmp/gw-capture.pcap
# observed lots of TCP RST from 10.9.2.14 -> backend IPs around 1918765440
```

Leila (sre): That aligns with ephemeral port exhaustion + refusals. Mitigation plan:
1) Add additional NAT gateway in another AZ (in progress).
2) Roll route table to spread subnets across NATs (done once NAT active).
3) If peering still flaps, escalate to AWS support with PCX logs (Mike).
4) If immediate customer impact persists, start traffic failover to hosted for critical customers (Ashley + Grace).

Mike (netops): I'm opening an AWS support case now (case 123456789) and attaching PCX logs and flow logs. Also suggested to AWS to check control plane event stream for the transit attachment.

Grace (support): Drafting a customer status update: "We're investigating intermittent 5xx errors for private inference. Engineers are mitigating and will provide updates in 30m." Shall I send?

Nina (oncall): Yes, send now. Include mitigation actions and ETA 30m. :+1:

netops-bot: create-nat(nat-1) completed in us-west-2a. NAT Gateway nat-1 created and available.

Nina (oncall): Updating route table to split subnets across nat-0a1b2c3d and nat-1. Patch applied to rtb-0c2d3e4f. Rolling now.

Ashley (eng): I'm enabling failover routing for a small percentage of weighted traffic to hosted as a safety net (5% traffic). Monitoring error rate.

Leila (sre): After route update the 5m error rate drops from 18% -> 6% within 2 minutes. Connection resets fall dramatically.

Mike (netops): AWS support reply: "We see peering control-plane retries coincident with heavy SNAT port usage causing connection resets. Recommend distributing NAT usage and increase rate limits or deploy secondary NAT per AZ." They've flagged the account for deeper review.

Grace (support): Customer update: Sent initial note and follow-up: "We implemented failover and are seeing decreased errors. Please contact support if you continue seeing failures. Will follow up once fully resolved."

Nina (oncall): Current status: Partial mitigation in place (new NAT + route split + 5% hosted fallback). Rolling error now ~1.2%. Keeping pager open until stabilized for 30m. Handing off to Mike for netops follow-up and to Ashley for longer-term remediation (connection pooling, NAT scaling).

Mike (netops): Taking post-incident action: schedule permanent NAT capacity increase, enable additional NATs per AZ, review peering stability with AWS, and validate any recent SG changes that could have amplified resets.

Ashley (eng): Postmortem owner: I'll own application-side mitigations (retry/backoff knobs, connection keepalive, probe tests).

Leila (sre): I'll draft incident timeline and RCA (conntrack/ephemeral port exhaustion causing control-plane peering flaps under load) and include remediation items.

Nina (oncall): Closing on-call shift: leaving notes in Ops handoff doc and marking incident as "Mitigated - Monitoring". Pager remains but risk reduced.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=high, summary="5xx spike from private-inference-gateway due to NAT port exhaustion and peering instability. Mitigations: added NAT, split routes, hosted fallback."

Leila (sre): Post-incident actions to add to RFC: permanent NAT per AZ, automatic NAT autoscale trigger on ActiveFlowCount, synthetic probes for VPC peering health, and guardrail for SG egress changes to prevent accidental lock-downs.

Grace (support): I'll compile customer impact numbers and ticket list for postmortem.

Nina (oncall): Great work team. Leaving handoff to Mike/Leila/Ashley. If anything spikes back up, re-paging. :thumbsup:
